translate_en|mods/SMB_TheySEEYou/42/medi: Kept only so old presets load. A confirmed world sound always starts at the sprinter's real position and floor; this value has no effect.
After a scream is confirmed, one vanilla world sound starts at the sprinter's real position. Any zombie type inside the radius may react. Disable for audio only.
Hearing radius for normal zombies and sprinters. This works only when attraction is enabled; larger values can move a larger horde.
Interval between chase-scream attempts for the same sprinter. 0.03 = 108 in-game seconds. Lower values are more vocal; real time follows day length.
One roll is made per eligible chase interval. 0 disables chase screams; 100 makes every eligible interval succeed. Identification is always guaranteed on target lock.
How long confirmed screams remain in the nearby-area budget. 0.01 = 36 in-game seconds; real time follows day length.
Nearby confirmed screams share an area budget. Larger values suppress more overlapping follow-up screams. The target-lock identification scream bypasses this limit.
Allows an extra scream when a sprinter enters within 8 tiles after being farther away. Disable it to reduce noise during close combat.

Allows sprinters without a locked target to scream occasionally while a player is within the encounter range. Disable it to keep only screams tied to target lock, the hunt, close range or a player shout.
Spontaneous presence screams and target-locked hunt screams can occur only while a player is within this distance. The full 10-300 tile range is supported.
Controls every scream except the close-range scream. 0.08 is recommended; 0.10 is normal level; values above 0.10 progressively amplify it up to 3x.
Multiplier applied to every mod voice. 1.0 keeps the intended mix; lower values soften it and higher values amplify it.
Number of confirmed screams the area can hold before follow-up screams are suppressed. Identification screams still occur, then quiet later screams nearby.
Limits how far away target-locked sprinters are fully evaluated. Spontaneous voices use the vocal range, so that range becomes the minimum automatically. Higher values may use more CPU.
Maximum confirmed screams in one hunt chapter. Identification or rediscovery starts a chapter; after 0.1 in-game hour, a silent sprinter can gain a second wind.
Kept only so old presets load. Every scream now plays from the actual sprinter's moving 3D source; this value has no effect.
Volume multiplier used only for close-range screams. 1.0 is normal; lower values soften them and higher values make them louder.
Maximum pitch offset assigned from each sprinter's stable identity. 0 keeps the source pitch; 7 allows up to +/-7%%. The same sprinter keeps its voice and pitch.
Chance of a distant presence scream (%%)
Rolled once whenever a distant presence scream becomes eligible. 0 prevents it; 100 preserves the original frequency. A failed roll waits for a new normal interval. Other scream types are unaffected.
Time without the target or clear sight before a rediscovery scream can occur. 0.04 = 144 in-game seconds; real time follows day length.
Kept only so old presets load. Identification occurs when a sprinter locks a player as its chase target; this value has no effect.
Allow sprinters to answer player shouts
Maximum distance for an eligible sprinter to answer. This works only when shout responses are enabled; area limits may reduce the number of replies.
A real player shout has only a limited chance of an answer, and at most one eligible sprinter responds. After answering, it stays silent for 0.4 in-game hour; repeated shouts cannot force replies.
Lower values react sooner and use more CPU; higher values spread the work and react later. 6 is recommended. Timing does not depend on frame rate.
0 = anytime; 1 = day and brighter twilight; 2 = night and darker twilight. Dawn and dusk change gradually.
